newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian right claims parliamentary majority.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian right claims parliamentary majority.

text.p: An alliance of three Slovenian rightwing parties said on Friday it had secured the extra vote in parliament it needed to form the next government.

The loose "Spring" alliance, comprising the People's Party, centre-right Social Democrats and Christian Democrats, won 45 out of 90 parliamentary seats in the November 10 general election, missing an absolute majority by just one seat.
"The 46th vote is no longer in question," Marjan Podobnik, head of the conservative People's Party and the "Spring" group's candidate for prime minister, told a news conference.

Podobnik, whose People's Party is the strongest in the alliance with 19 seats, refused to reveal who would supply the crucial vote. He said talks aimed at beefing up a coalition government were still continuing.
"I see no problems in forming the government, the only question is whether we will have a simple or a two-thirds majority," he said.

Podobnik declined to speculate on who would be given the first crack at forming a government. President Milan Kucan has to name a candidate within 30 days of the first parliamentary session, set for November 28.
The "Spring" parties are up against the centre-left Liberal Democrats of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, who are the strongest single party with 25 seats.
The "Spring" alliance approached the Liberal Democrats after the election to offer them a place in government if Drnovsek stepped down as premier, but they refused.
Podobnik said his government would be in favour of Slovenia joining the European Union and NATO although the new administration would ensure that national interests came first.
Slovenia, which declared independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991, hopes to join NATO by 1999 and the EU by 2001. This month's election was the second since independence.
